To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rheological parameters of the blood fluid are not of relevance for the erythrocytes velocity in human nail fold capillaries under normal resting conditions but that the plasma viscosity is the most important parameter of blood fluidity determining the erythrocytic velocity during vessel paralysis in the postischemia of the nail fold capillar.

under normal conditions the erythrocytes are transported through the microvessels in a very efficient way, so that the velocity is only dependent on the local perfusion pressure, and that the blood fluidity has no effect on the erythrocytic velocity.

the erythrocytes in capillaries of healthy subjects move at a mean velocity of 1.5 mm/s under resting conditions and that the plasma viscosity and erythrocytes aggregation are decisive factors for the regulation of the blood flow in the capillaries of the nailfold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of rheological parameters (plasma viscosity and erythrocytes) on the velocity of the erythrocytes in nailfold capillaroscopy.
the question whether the blood fluidity influences the velocity of erythrocyes in human nailfold microvessels.
the influence of rheological parameters of blood on the erythrocytic velocity in human nail-fold capillaries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plasma viscosity is an important factor in determining the erythrocytes' velocity passing capillaries under physiological and pathological conditions.
under normal conditions the blood flow regulation is so effective that no correlation between rheology and capillary perfusion can be found.
plasma viscosity is a decisive factor for the regulation of the microcirculation in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the erythrocytes velocity in capillares is determined by the plasma viscosity and that the erythroocyte aggregation plays a role only under certain conditions.
under resting conditions the erythrocytes in capillaries are flowing with a maximum velocity which is determined by the blood fluidity.
the erythrocytes are not able to pass the capillaries faster than the plasma flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plasma viscosity is the most important rheological parameter influencing the velocity of an individual erythrocyte in human capillaries.

in humans the erythrocytic flow in nailfold capillariies seems to be regulated in such a way that even in pathological conditions the erythrocytes pass the capillaries at a velocity similar to that of healthy subjects.
rheological parameters are not important for the capillary perfuion under physiological conditions, but during vessel paralysis.
